scope: sources_48_recheck; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Malformed `from` field in a delta row raises raw AttributeError/TypeError from `row.get('from',{}).get(...)`, not the typed StorageError path in all shapes
findings.issue: `_mail_metadata` guards `sender` isinstance-str and wraps `ValueError/TypeError/KeyError/AttributeError`, but `row.get('from',{})` can be `None` (JSON null), which makes `.get('emailAddress',{})` raise `AttributeError` inside the `try` — this is caught. However `row` itself can be a non-dict (e.g. a string) in `fetch_page`/`sync` after the per-row `isinstance(row,dict)` check in `sync` is present but `fetch_page` (graph.py:213) calls `_mail_metadata(row)` before any `isinstance(row,dict)` validation, so a non-dict row produces `AttributeError` on `row.get` that is caught and re-raised as StorageError — acceptable. The real residual defect is that `read_message` (graph.py:254-255) parses `receivedDateTime` and nested `from` with no shape validation at all: `datetime.fromisoformat(value['receivedDateTime']...)` raises raw ValueError/KeyError and `value.get('from',{}).get(...)` raises AttributeError on a null `from`, escaping as untyped exceptions rather than a denied/typed error.
findings.fix: Route `read_message`'s `receivedDateTime`/`from` parsing through `_mail_metadata` (or equivalent typed validation) so malformed provider shapes raise `StorageError`/`CapabilityDenied` rather than leaking raw `ValueError`/`AttributeError`. Add a null/`from`-non-dict case to the malformed-metadata test beyond `[]`.

findings.title: Graph cursor records are never consumed and `version=1` is not enforced as an expected version
findings.issue: `self.store.get(request.owner_ref,'conversation',request.cursor,version=1)` passes `version=1` but the code only checks payload equality and never increments/deletes the cursor on use, so the same opaque cursor ref remains valid indefinitely and can be replayed across requests for the same selection scope. This is read-only pagination, not one-use write confirmation, so it is not by itself an authorization bypass (scope/connection binding and a fresh grant are still required per call), but it lacks any expiry or single-use bound.
findings.fix: Add an explicit expiry or consume-on-read version fence for stored cursors, and validate the stored record's expected version rather than ignoring `version=1`. Keep the existing per-call scope/connection/authorization checks as the primary guard.

not_verified: `prm.storage.postgres` `get`/`put` version semantics and whether `version=1` is treated as an expected-version filter (implementation not in packet).
`prm.capabilities` grant decode/authorize logic and `abandon_before_transport` semantics (referenced only).
Whether `read_message`'s untyped `datetime.fromisoformat` path is reachable with a malformed provider row in the synthetic fixtures (fixtures not supplied).
findings.summary: The packet covers the connection/credential, Graph, academic, and policy layers plus two test files and the #48 review receipt. Fail-closed behavior is generally strong: token refresh commits a durable `awaiting_refresh` fence before network I/O and marks unknown outcomes non-retryable, `cleanup_retired` never deletes a ref that is any account's active `secret_ref` (the cross-owner counterexample test confirms retention), grants are provider/purpose/connection-bound, and unknown pricing is denied rather than zeroed. Resolving #48's cited items independently: the cursor P1 is not a fail-open authorization defect, since read-only pagination is not one-use write confirmation and each call still revalidates owner/connection/selection and obtains a fresh reservation — but cursors do lack expiry/consumption (P2). The credential-cleanup P1 is refuted by the supplied counterexample test: the global active-secret check is intentionally cross-owner and correctly prevents deleting any live token; the suggested owner-scoped fix would be unsafe. The `from`/date typing fix holds for `_mail_metadata` (including the `from: []` case), but `read_message` still parses `receivedDateTime`/`from` without typed validation and can raise raw `ValueError`/`AttributeError` on malformed rows (P1). With no P0 and one P1, verdict is FIX_P1_FIRST.
